page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-4 is a compute-focused virtual server based on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, which contains 2 physical cores and supports 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. This server does not include any local NVMe storage, GPU hardware, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core benchmarks ranking in the top 25% at 2688.77, and Geekbench single-core scores reaching an average tier of 1464.0. Conversely, multi-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng multi-core (5394.87) and Geekbench multi-core (3311.0) scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also a bottleneck; the PassMark memory score of 1081.99 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 19.78 GB/sec both rank in the bottom 10% of tested hardware.

Given its hardware profile, the n2d-highcpu-4 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but have minimal memory requirements. The 1:1 ratio of RAM to vCPUs makes it poorly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale software compilation, or parallelized multi-threaded tasks. Instead, this instance is best utilized for single-threaded applications, basic text processing, lightweight web serving, and simple utility scripts.
